verdict.rationale: Letta's headless CLI mode is explicitly designed to be scripted and composed with other UNIX tools or CI/CD pipelines, which lets an AI-native user loop over many agents/tasks and drive bulk operations indirectly (letta-docs-4, letta-docs-13, letta-docs-37). However, there is no documented native bulk API — e.g. no batch-create/batch-update/batch-delete endpoint for agents, memory blocks, or shared-memory repos — so bulk operations rely entirely on external scripting rather than a first-class Letta feature. Missing for 10: a documented bulk/batch API or SDK method operating on multiple agents/items in a single call, evidence of bulk memory or shared-memory operations, and any hands-on confirmation that scripted bulk workflows actually work at scale.
